headline: Meta's spending outlook turned the bounce into a rout: semis -6.0%, optics -10.8%, and the market is now asking who pays for the build-out, not whether demand exists.
regime: Every AI segment fell hard (semis ETF -6.0% on the day, -13.0% on the month; networking/optical -10.8%; foundry equipment -9.0%) while the Nasdaq lost 2.6% and the VIX rose to 19.7. The 10-year yield dipped to 4.95% as money fled to Treasuries, which is risk-off rather than relief, and crude at $100 (Brent near $115 in headlines) keeps inflation and rates a threat. The shock is financing: BofA flags investor reluctance to fund AI infrastructure and OpenAI cut its valuation target, while orders still look fine (Western Digital beat, hardware demand intact). Only ai_software (-1.8%) held up.

theses.title: Power, grid and cooling, not chips, limit the AI build-out
evidence: Vertiv and Nvidia target a 10-week cut in AI power and cooling set-up time, so deployment speed is the constraint being attacked (7e8e1943fe55)
Musk says AI is short on power (d6da5e143d40)
Eaton is getting upward earnings revisions even after a 6% drop (f3eaf91f024f, 963998a389ad)
theses.change_note: -3: the constraint is intact, but grid equipment fell 8.2% on the day (GEV -11%, PWR -8%, POWL -11%) because financing, not physical scarcity, is now the binding risk.

theses.title: AI compute demand still outruns supply
evidence: Western Digital beat revenue expectations on AI storage demand (2d3d9963978a)
Nebius says GPU rental prices keep running ahead of plan (9e1871791046)
AMD has booked gigawatts of accelerator commitments with 50% revenue growth (447a42693de8)
theses.change_note: -6: orders are fine, but OpenAI cutting its valuation target by $150B (d6cbed05b021) shows the end-customer funding can shrink, and stocks sold off on good numbers.

theses.title: Debt-funded neoclouds are where the AI cycle breaks first
evidence: CoreWeave, NuScale and others hit 52-week lows on debt fears (82492ea6fadf)
Nebius borrowed $3.5B and the terms suggest it is buying time (9e1871791046)
The segment is down 29.8% on the month and 11.2% over five days (digest tape)
theses.change_note: +6: new 52-week lows and another large borrowing; Goldman's upgrade of CoreWeave (d835ba8e2de5) is one voice against a falling tape.

theses.title: Memory is priced as if this is the peak of the cycle
evidence: Western Digital beat estimates handily and the stock still did not respond (976b6e96d1df)
SK Hynix scrapped its US IPO of the memory unit, read as a warning signal for the AI trade (1e74e44c3cbf)
The segment is down 26.6% on the month, SOXX and DRAM down 24-42% from highs (f5412226b26f)
theses.change_note: -3: good results met no buying again and the SK Hynix IPO pull suggests funding appetite is thinning; cheap multiples still limit the downside.

theses.title: Hyperscaler capex is eating their free cash flow
evidence: Meta led the AI rout (down about 7%, -11.9% over five days) as its spending outlook left financing unanswered (8e61083f95a7, 8439969405c6)
BofA sees growing investor reluctance to fund AI infrastructure (b62e92569b9b)
Bond market is warning on the AI infrastructure build-out (62ac909d0520)
theses.change_note: +11: the market reacted to capex for the first time as a funding problem, which is the thesis.

theses.title: The AI trade is crowded and rates are high
evidence: Nasdaq fell below its 50-day line, semis -6.0% in a day (0a1526ef7f42)
Retail sentiment on SPY and DIA was extremely bearish premarket (2a09212edcdc)
Yields at 4.95% with oil at five-month highs keep the discount rate high (514df5a01d41, 1485421369dd)
theses.change_note: +7: a 6% single-day semis drop is what crowded positioning unwinding looks like; the yield fall is a flight to safety, not a relief.

compute.note: Down 16.7% on the month; demand is real but no price floor until financing worries ease.

foundry_equipment.note: Worst 5d move after optics at -10.8%; cyclical and crowded.

memory_storage.note: Down 26.6% on the month on single-digit forward P/Es (WDC 9.6x); downside is cushioned if the cycle holds.

networking_optical.note: -10.8% on the day, -21.7% on the month with Coherent -12%; no valuation cushion.

servers.note: Dell -6.8%; HPE at 11.8x forward earnings is the only cheap entry but margins are thin.

power_nuclear.note: Keep to cash-generating producers; pre-revenue nuclear is falling hardest (LEU -18% over five days).

grid_electrical.note: Physical bottleneck intact, selling is financing fear; prefer profitable names with estimate upgrades such as Eaton.

cooling_thermal.note: Vertiv/Nvidia deployment speed-up and nVent's AMD cooling deal; Vertiv and Modine report soon.

datacenter_neocloud.note: 52-week lows and rising debt; avoid until financing clears.

hyperscalers.note: Capex is now being punished (Meta -11.9% in five days); wait for funding clarity.

ai_software.note: Held up (-1.8%, flat on the month) but is momentum, not a bottleneck play.

risks: Further AI funding doubts (OpenAI valuation cut, BofA warning) could cut capex plans and hit the whole supplier chain.
Oil near $100-115 on Middle East conflict could keep inflation and yields elevated.
A VIX rising toward 20 and Nasdaq below its 50-day line point to forced selling in crowded names.
Neocloud debt stress (CoreWeave, Nebius) could spread to GPU, power and cooling suppliers through cancelled orders.
Memory earnings may be at peak cycle; SK Hynix pulling its IPO is a warning.
watch: Whether the Micron-led chip rebound holds on Monday after the Friday bounce.
Amazon earnings on Oct. 29 for a read on capex and financing.
Vertiv, GE Vernova and Modine earnings for power and cooling demand.
CoreWeave and Nebius funding costs and their 52-week lows.
The 10-year yield against 5% and the Fed meeting.
